hints: Focus on what being in the same Period tells you about electron shells, and what changes as you move left to right.
Remember atomic radius decreases across Period 3, so the atom with the larger radius must sit to the left of the smaller one.
Since X is already a non-metal on the right side of Period 3, think about what type of element must lie even further to its right.
walkthrough:
**Place X and Y in Period 3**

Both atoms are in Period 3, so both have electrons in three occupied shells. Neither is argon, so we are looking at $\text{Na}$ to $\text{Cl}$.

Rule across a period:
$$\text{atomic radius decreases left to right}$$

**Use the radius clue to order X and Y**

X has a greater atomic radius than Y. Across a period, greater radius means lower nuclear charge and a position further left.

So in the Periodic Table:
$$\text{X is to the left of Y}$$

**Use the non-metal clue**

X is a non-metal, so X must be on the right side of Period 3, such as $\text{P}$, $\text{S}$ or $\text{Cl}$. But X is to the left of Y, and Y is even further right (but not argon).

That means Y must also be in the non-metal block on the right, for example if X is $\text{P}$ then Y could be $\text{S}$ or $\text{Cl}$.

options.A: Incorrect. Same period means same number of occupied shells. Both X and Y are in Period 3, so both have 3 occupied shells.
options.B: Incorrect. Proton number increases left to right across a period. Since X is to the left of Y (larger radius), X has fewer protons than Y, not more.
options.C: Incorrect. They are different elements in the same period, so they are in different groups and have different numbers of outer shell electrons.
options.D: Correct. X is a non-metal on the right of Period 3 and lies to the left of Y. The only elements to the right of P, S (excluding argon) are also non-metals, so Y must be a non-metal too.
